target_role: Technical Project Manager — Product Operations & Implementation, especially for civic technology or other public-facing teams.
central_value: Turns ambiguous, stakeholder-heavy work into usable operating structure: requirements, workflows, decision records, documentation, launch support, onboarding, and durable handoffs.
proof_examples: Modernized web, e-commerce, analytics, content, marketing, and operational workflows for an 80-plus-year-old industrial business, contributing to reported 2x revenue growth.

Created 30-plus pages of campaign-memory infrastructure for FairRentNYC/NYC Artist Coalition, including action trackers, source maps, policy-question logs, stakeholder follow-up, and a provenance redline.
Built CallNYC.org as an independent CouncilStat follow-on that translated constituent-services data into resident-facing issue pages and next-step guidance.
Co-built WOWList using Django, PostgreSQL/PostGIS, and Ember; the community-calendar platform reportedly reached roughly 35 city ecosystems.
Created repeatable onboarding, facilitation, documentation, and continuity systems supporting 300-plus gatherings and 20-plus resident artists.
next_action: Advance Jamie to a first-round screen and ask for a walkthrough of one civic-tech implementation: the problem, personal ownership, cross-functional dependencies, measurable outcome, and handoff.
invented_claims: I could not determine whether Jamie has held a formal Technical Project Manager title; the materials establish the target role and relevant work, but provide no employment chronology or job titles.

I could not support people-management, budget, procurement, contracting, security, or legal decision authority. Coordination across some of these functions is asserted, but formal authority is not demonstrated.
The 2x revenue contribution, 35-city reach, and other scale metrics are self-reported here and cannot be independently verified from these three files.
I could not determine the current production status, user volume, or service impact of CallNYC or WOWList.
rationale: The two-minute criterion is met. The opening immediately names the role and repeats a memorable central promise. Multiple distinct projects provide concrete civic, technical, operational, and community proof, while the application offers an obvious route to the resume and contact. Some metrics and authority boundaries need interview verification, but understanding the candidacy does not require inventing either.
